newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's PT gathers enough votes for scandal probe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's PT gathers enough votes for scandal probe.

text.p: A left-wing Brazilian political party has gathered enough signatures for a parliamentary inquiry into an alleged cash-for-votes scam, but still requires votes on the floor of the house to set up the probe, an official said.

"We've got more than enough signatures. Now we have to approve a motion which will actually set the CPI up," said a Workers Party (PT) spokesman. CPI is the Portuguese acronym for a Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry, or a Congressional probe.
Left-wing parties are trying to set up two CPIs, one just in the Chamber of Deputies and another in both houses of Congress.
More than 190 members of the Chamber of Deputies had already signed their support for both inquiries, more than enough for the lower house probe, the official said.
PT lawmakers were due to ask the president of the Chamber of Deputies to give priority treatment to a resolution that would allow that probe to be set up immediately, he said.
Five CPIs are officially under way in the lower house, the maximum normally allowed at any one time.

But if the resolution was approved on the lower house floor, by a majority of a session attended by at least half the house's 513 members, the new probe would be allowed to "jump the queue," the official said.
Regarding the mixed, two-house CPI, PT lawmakers were trying to persuade senators to lend their signatures to a petition calling for the inquiry, he said.
Earlier Wednesday, Deputy Inocencio Oliveira told reporters the government wanted to avoid any CPI into the allegations, arguing an inquiry of that sort would "paralise" Congress.
An internal congressional panel is currently investigating the reports.
